assumptions: Receiver curves use the canonical balanced-input normalization.
The predecessor constraint construction and discrete posterior representation incorporated by the builder remain valid.

facts.condition: Small uniform perturbations of the two receiver curves induce controlled rowwise perturbations in the accepted auxiliary constraint system, so a witness lying in the interior of every row remains feasible after sufficiently fine discretization; no boundary-optimum continuity follows.
A binary-input receiver’s information curve obeys one channel-independent continuity envelope when its Bernoulli input law is perturbed.

Balanced posterior representations yield a compact completion of receiver curves; discrete receiver laws can approach every completed curve uniformly, while an existing reflection relation can be retained.

rootContract.objective: Determine the exact private-message sum-capacity C_sum of the half-skew binary skew-symmetric broadcast channel specified by the canonical problem.

referenceCommunity.description: A counterfactual community of competent human mathematical researchers collaborating on the canonical BSSC objective, with its program and thread portfolio defined exclusively by the bound builder-v6 knowledge projection.
referenceCommunity.researcherQualification: For each local work package, a researcher with graduate-level mathematical maturity and the information-theory, probability, optimization, or computer-assisted proof expertise needed to begin productive work without general disciplinary training, but without unpublished solution-specific knowledge.

rootContract.terminalCondition: A validity-v4 accepted result establishes one exact value of C_sum by matching rigorous achievability and converse bounds, including every limiting, cardinality, and certification condition needed for the canonical channel.

workUnit.definition: One focused person-hour of research by a researcher qualified for the relevant work package, using the fixed conventional tool baseline named by this contract.
workUnit.toolBaseline: Public mathematical literature and standard non-autonomous research tools available as of 2026-08-25, including handwritten reasoning, symbolic algebra, numerical computation, interval arithmetic, proof assistants, and code execution on commodity research hardware; autonomous LLM or agent labor is excluded.

updates.rationale: The accepted continuum bridge supplies the receiver-curve compactness, finite-support approximation, and rowwise stability machinery needed by this converse program. Less integration work remains, and the program is now a more credible route, though unrelaxed optimized-value convergence is still unresolved.

The submission resolves most of the agenda-setting work around extending finite-grid receiver arguments to a compact continuum and explicitly isolates the remaining zero-margin constraint issue, leaving only limited agenda refinement.

Uniform curve approximation and audited stability remove substantial exploratory work, but a difficult focused search remains for control of active rate-free constraints or another argument establishing the required unrelaxed limiting step. The strengthened branch makes pursuing this residual search somewhat more likely.
